items.title: 68357_Jimmy Maxwell oral history interview
items.q: the contractor, Lou Shobe Shubey's stickler for punctuality

ctx.x: they're not going to be hired again if they do these things. I don't care how much they want to, quote, do their thing or express themselves. When you're working for a guy, you may not like his rules but those are the rules and he's hiring you and you'd better follow them if you want to work.

Right, I agree. I can remember being the recipient of that once. I -- for so long I had been working with all of you guys in the studios, recording studios where we came in sneakers and jeans because we were in a recording studio. And I remember once I got a call for a radio show, which was -- you know, there wouldn't be no audience there, just a radio show in a studio. And of course I went just like I went to the recording session. And I remember it was at CBS, and I think the big detail, when I went there and…
go, as you say, when you're going in that part of town in that particular society, then you act like that.
